Refused
rē-fūzd´
v. (declined, rejected; rendering Hebrew ma'en, ma'as, Greek arneomai, paraiteomai)
From Latin refusare, to pour back, decline. Scripture uses the word for the noblest refusal in Hebrews 11 and for the most fatal refusal in Proverbs 1.

Biblical Definition

Refusal in Scripture cuts in both directions, and everything depends on what is refused. There is a refusal that is faith's finest act: “By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter” (Heb 11:24) — a man declining a throne because he had seen something better. There is the refusal that condemned the builders and became the cornerstone of the gospel: “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner” (Psa 118:22), quoted by Christ against the chief priests and by Peter before the Sanhedrin. There is the refusal wisdom warns of: “Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded” (Pro 1:24) — and the chapter goes on to a silence that answers in kind. And Hebrews presses the point to its sharpest edge: “See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven” (Heb 12:25).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines refuse as to deny a request, demand or invitation; to decline to accept an offer; and to reject, to decline to do or grant.

expand to see more

REFUSE, v.t. To deny a request, demand, invitation or command; to decline to do or grant.

2. To decline to accept what is offered; as, to refuse an office.

3. To reject; to dismiss.

REFUSE, v.i. To decline to accept; not to comply.

REFUSED, pp. Denied; rejected; not accepted.

Key Scripture

Heb 11:24 — "By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter;"

Psa 118:22 — "The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner."

Pro 1:24 — "Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded;"

Heb 12:25 — "See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven:"

Modern Corruption

Refusal is treated as inherently negative — closed-mindedness, exclusion — where Scripture makes the direction of the refusal the whole question, and honours Moses for the greatest No in the Old Testament.

expand to see more

A culture whose highest virtue is openness has trouble with a Bible that praises a man for saying no. Hebrews 11 lists Moses' refusal among the great acts of faith: he declined the standing, wealth, and identity that Egypt held out, choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season. That is not narrowness; it is arithmetic, and Hebrews shows his working — he had respect unto the recompence of the reward. Every faithful refusal in Scripture is made by someone who has priced both options.

Proverbs 1 and Hebrews 12 supply the terrible symmetry. The man who refuses wisdom's call will one day call and not be answered; the man who refuses Him that speaketh from heaven has no second court of appeal. And Psalm 118 shows what happens to the thing men refuse: the rejected stone becomes the head of the corner. Refusal does not dispose of Christ. It only determines whether a man meets Him as foundation or as the stone that falls.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew ma'en (H3985), to refuse, and ma'as (H3988), to reject or despise; Greek arneomai (G720), to deny, and paraiteomai (G3868), to decline or beg off.

expand to see more

Hebrew ma'as (H3988) — to refuse, reject, despise; “the stone which the builders refused” (Psa 118:22).

Hebrew ma'en (H3985) — to refuse, be unwilling; “I have called, and ye refused” (Pro 1:24).

Greek arneomai (G720) — to deny, disown, refuse; Moses refusing the name of Pharaoh's daughter (Heb 11:24).

Usage

"“Refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter” — faith declining a throne."

"“The stone which the builders refused” — refusal did not dispose of Him."

"“See that ye refuse not him that speaketh” — and there is no higher court."
